subject: TheraHealth: private VPC control-link fluctuation — proposed mitigations & evidence

Cc: sre-oncall@therahealth.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brief outage window — control-plane flaps on our TheraHealth private deployment

Hi Naomi,

We observed intermittent control-plane connectivity drops between 17:24 and 17:46 PDT today that resulted in ~90s delays for several inference requests and a handful of 504s. We rolled our app to a fallback model briefly which mitigated user-visible failures, but token costs jumped and latency variance spiked.

Attached are the connection traces and a short timeline from our side. Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's end around that window (agent upgrade, orchestration churn, or routing policy changes)? We are preparing an internal incident report and procurement wants a quick summary for their risk log.

Thanks — Julie
---
Julie Nguyen
SRE Lead, TheraHealth
julie.nguyen@therahealth.com

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 18:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Brief outage window — control-plane flaps on our TheraHealth private deployment

Julie — thanks for the heads up and the traces. We saw a small spike in control-link retries for a subset of TheraHealth agents at roughly 17:23–17:48 PDT coincident with a staged controlplane tooling rollout from our side. The rollout targeted a telemetry serialization change that should have been backward-compatible, but one older agent variant did not honor the new heartbeat pacing and produced transient backpressure.

Immediate actions taken:
- Scoped the rollout and paused the remaining fleet rollouts at 17:35 PDT.
- Pushed an automatic fallback to the previous agent build for the affected agent pool at 17:40 PDT.
- Enabled extra diagnostic tracing for the TheraHealth tenant (you should see more verbose logs in the attached archive).

Next steps we propose:
1) We will prepare a short post-incident summary and share traces/evidence by EOD tomorrow.
2) If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min bridge with your SREs and our runtime team to walk the artifacts and confirm the rollback.
3) Recommend a coordinated maintenance window to rerun the rollout after we back-merge a compatibility guard.

I have looped in Marcus (runtime lead) and Marissa (customer ops) to coordinate. Apologies for the disruption — we know TheraHealth traffic is sensitive.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: TheraHealth: control-link fluctuation — triage notes

Quick triage notes from runtime: the telemetry push introduced a 250ms aggregate delay in heartbeat ack processing on older linux-agent-1.8.x instances under burst load. That delay resulted in 2–3 consecutive retry windows being fired which the agent treated as intermittent connectivity. Not a token-processing regression, but controlplane link jitter.

Proposed mitigation (short term): automatic guard that enforces older heartbeat pacing for tenants with agent variants <1.9, plus a hotfix to remove the problematic batching of telemetry ACKs. We can stage the hotfix to a canary group (5% of hosts) for 48 hours, then gradually expand.

Irene — can you prepare the rollback playbook and evidence bundle we should send to the customer (logs, control-plane traces, canary rollout plan)? Naomi — I can be on the bridge if TheraHealth wants it.

— Marcus
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: julie.nguyen@therahealth.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TheraHealth: private VPC control-link fluctuation — rollback playbook & evidence

Hi Julie / team — attaching our preliminary postmortem draft and the trimmed log bundle with the key traces called out. Short summary up front:
- Root cause: compatibility regression in telemetry serialization causing delayed heartbeat ACKs on linux-agent-1.8.x under burst conditions.
- Customer impact: elevated latency variance and a small number of 504s during 17:24–17:46 PDT; no data exfiltration or model-state corruption observed.
- Immediate remediation completed: paused rollout and rolled back affected agents at 17:40 PDT.

Action items for shared runbook:
- Schedule a 30-minute bridge to review traces (we propose Mon 8 Mar 09:00 PDT).
- Coordinate a maintenance window for a guarded canary hotfix (48 hours staging at 5% hosts, then 25% -> 100% if green).
- Post-fix, we'll run a synthetic prefix workload to validate heartbeat behavior across your agent fleet.

Please see the attached postmortem-draft-thera-v1.docx and the trace archive for the specific evidence markers. Let us know if you want a customer-facing postmortem in a specific template — we can adapt.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Runtime Reliability — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
